title: Artifact entrant conversion harness and runtime compatibility sweep
creator: Liam Chen
description: Build a repeatable, auditable pipeline (the entrant harness) that converts an incoming community model artifact into validated runtime artifacts and publishes a performance profile + version anchor. This ticket covers conversion orchestration, deterministic validation checks, a compatibility sweep across representative hardware kernels, and the automation to publish a version anchor and profile into the model catalog. Aim is to reduce manual QA and shorten time-to-publish for new OSS LLM arrivals.
acceptance_criteria: Entrant harness runs end-to-end on new artifact and produces standard artifact bundle (model binary, metadata manifest, format marker)
Deterministic validation: artifact hash, layer type check, param counts match manifest; failures produce human-readable diagnostics
Compatibility sweep executes across CPU, GPU (A100/RTX family), and quantized variants; summary metrics (latency P50/P95, memory peak, token throughput) generated
Performance profile generated and stored in catalog with version anchor tag 'anchor-<model>-<semver>'
Automated smoke tests: generation with three prompts and token-level checksum tolerances pass for approved variant
Publish step creates audit entry and links to produced artifacts + performance dashboard
plan_steps: 1) Define entrant harness contract and standardized artifact bundle spec (manifest fields, checksum algorithm, conversion flags)
2) Implement conversion adapters for major formats (torch checkpoint, safetensors, hf repo snapshot -> internal runtime format)
3) Add deterministic validators: weight shape checks, RNG independence, non-fused op detection
4) Wire compatibility sweep: matrix runner that spins small-scale jobs on target kernels and records metrics
5) Attach heuristics for quantization recommendation and profile annotations
6) Create anchor-and-publish automation to write canonical model version + profile to catalog and emit telemetry
7) End-to-end smoke & canary: run entrant harness against 5 community models and iterate on failures
test_plan: Unit tests for conversion adapters and manifest parsing
Deterministic validation tests using synthesized artifacts that exercise mismatch/error branches
Integration tests that exercise full harness on a tiny distilled model in CI
Compatibility sweep acceptance criteria validated by running on infra-provisioned nodes in staging and recording SLO-crossing alerts
Manual QA checklist: review profile graphs, inspect produced manifest and anchor, run generation samples
rollback_and_risks: Risk: conversion can produce silent numerical drift causing downstream regressions. Mitigation: strict smoke prompts + token-level tolerance and manual sign-off for drift > threshold
Risk: hardware kernel mismatch for new op patterns. Mitigation: early abort on unknown ops and automatic routing to fallback implementation + ticket creation
Rollback: anchor publishing is an atomic operation; if post-publish regressions detected, automation will tag 'anchor-<model>-reverted-<ts>' and re-point catalog to previous anchor
Risk: storage/quota limits in staging during sweep. Mitigation: ephemeral cleanup job and artifact retention TTL of 72h in staging
